shouldFix.title: recordedInputs.governingSources pins COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md at a digest four adopted decisions stale, with no authoring-time qualifier
shouldFix.provenance: I walked all 95 committed revisions of the file. The pinned digest reproduces exactly at commit 2327cf8 (D-100), so it was valid when written and has since gone stale through D-103, D-104, D-105 and D-106. This is staleness, not fabrication.
shouldFix.why: The entry is labelled a pin and carries a load-bearing role: 'D-002 advertises SARIF for analyze only and rides DR-006; D-077 owner-records DR-006 preview disposition that DROPS SARIF_for_analyze from the preview; D-086/D-092 record G17 inapplicable.' That citation is the warrant for this artifact's entire preview posture - the applicability law, the SARIF-dropped standing, and the G17-inapplicable claim. A reviewer re-measuring at the pinned bytes gets a mismatch, so the warrant cannot be checked as recorded. The artifact's two other source pins (file 01, file 08) are both current, so the surrounding convention reads as live-accurate pinning rather than snapshot pinning. This chain has twice treated a non-reproducing pin as a MUST-FIX on the decision side (CLAUDE-D106-M1, CODEX-D106T2-M1) on the principle that a recorded measurement which does not reproduce is not a measurement.
shouldFix.whyNotABlocker: The substance survives intact. I confirmed D-002, D-077, D-086 and D-092 are all still present in the live file - COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md only grew by appended decisions, and nothing the role cites was altered or removed. No claim in the artifact is false; only the pin is out of date.
shouldFix.notIntroducedHere: recordedInputs is byte-identical to v5 - it appears in neither the changed, added, nor removed set of my v5-to-v6 diff - so v6 inherited this pin rather than introducing it. That is consistent with basedOn.method's closure sentence, but inheriting an assertion does not make a stale assertion current, and v6 is dated 2026-08-15, the same day D-106 was adopted, so the pin was already behind at authoring.
shouldFix.remedy: Either re-measure to 39f372e1e1031a67de132b311b463e18e0deca9224afdb085754e30c4540aac0 in a v7, or adopt the qualifier the sibling contract in this corpus already uses - lifecycle-generation-contract.v2 marks an inherited pin with measuredAtV1Authoring true, standing INHERITED-V*, and the sentence 'The pin is not a this-authoring whole-document claim.' Either closes it. The second is the more durable fix because it closes the class for every governingSources entry rather than this instance.

repairVerification.finding: CODEX-V5-B1 - inputOutcomeLaw must bind advertisement/DR-006 standing to exactly one arm with a truthful expected.reason, and not-produced must forbid sarif+ACTIVE
howIChecked: I enumerated the state space rather than reading the prose. advertisement and dr006Standing are both closed enums on the not-produced arm ({none, sarif} and {INACTIVE, ACTIVE}), giving exactly four states. inputOutcomeLaw.table maps each to exactly one arm: (none, INACTIVE) and (none, ACTIVE) to not-produced/preview-not-advertised, (sarif, INACTIVE) to not-produced/dr006-inactive, (sarif, ACTIVE) to produced/null. No state is unmapped and none maps twice.

The forbidden combination is blocked in three independent places, so no single edit can reopen it: inputOutcomeLaw.forbidden names it explicitly; inputNotProduced.forbids states 'advertisement=sarif AND dr006Standing=ACTIVE is forbidden on this arm; that state is inputProduced only'; and inputNotProduced.lawfulCombinations enumerates only the two lawful pairings, omitting it structurally rather than by prose.

The produced arm is closed from the other direction: inputProduced constrains advertisement to the single-value enum {sarif} and dr006Standing to {ACTIVE}, so that arm cannot be selected for any other state.

Truthfulness of reason is enforced two ways: expectedWhenNotProduced.reason is a closed enum of exactly the two lawful values, and reasonBinding requires expected.reason to equal the expectedReason that inputOutcomeLaw assigns to the selected advertisement/standing, which rules out the enum-valid but untruthful pairing of (none, INACTIVE) with dr006-inactive.

I considered whether reasonBinding being prose rather than a JSON-Schema if/then is a gap. It is not one I can charge here: lawfulCombinations is structured data an implementation consumes directly, the artifact is a DESIGN-CONTRACT-CANDIDATE that reserves mechanism by design, and requiring a schema encoding would be a stronger demand than the finding made.

repairVerification.finding: CODEX-V5-S1 - nativeMappings must keep the result index distinct from the location index, make the primary locations[0], and preserve relatedLocations order
howIChecked: The index conflation is gone and the distinction is now stated rather than implied: a new resultIndex key defines 'r is the index of the result in run.results[]', primaryLocationUri is run.results[r].locations[0].physicalLocation.artifactLocation.uri - a literal 0, not r - and relatedLocationUri uses an independent index k over run.results[r].relatedLocations[k].

placementRule pins the ordering to a named source: the additional URIs are 'the preserved canonical host artifact-ref order from the host result (the same order as result.properties.opensip.artifactRefs excluding the primary URI)'. That is an order defined against host data, not left to the emitter.

It also closes the two adjacent escapes: 'One URI occupies exactly one of those two roles per result' forbids double-placement, and 'There is no and-join and no permutation freedom' forbids the unordered reading. Per-entry NFC normalization and the note that native placement does not replace opensip.artifactRefs identity both survive.

attacksAttemptedAndFailed.attack: A not-produced arm that still permits advertisement=sarif and dr006Standing=ACTIVE
attacksAttemptedAndFailed.detail: Blocked at inputOutcomeLaw.forbidden, at inputNotProduced.forbids, and structurally by lawfulCombinations omitting the pair. inputProduced's single-value enums make (sarif, ACTIVE) reachable only on the produced arm. Both governing enums are closed, so there is no fifth state to exploit.

attacksAttemptedAndFailed.attack: nativeMappings that still conflate result index with locations[i] or leave relatedLocations unordered
attacksAttemptedAndFailed.detail: Primary is a literal locations[0]; related use an independent k; resultIndex defines r explicitly; related order is pinned to host artifact-ref order excluding the primary; permutation freedom and and-joins are both denied by name.

I flattened both generations to leaf paths and diffed: 39 added, 6 removed, 11 changed, 56 total. I then tested every one of the 56 against basedOn.method's eleven-path closed roster. All 56 are covered, including the 26 goldenShape additions, which fall entirely inside the rostered inputOutcomeLaw, inputNotProduced and inputProduced/requiresLaw subtrees. Notably /date did not change at all and is on the roster anyway, so this chain carries none of the unrostered-date residue seen elsewhere in this corpus. The one removal worth naming is /appliesFindingsOf/codexv4: it is inside the rostered /appliesFindingsOf subtree, honestyRepairsFromV4 is retained, and the dropped pin stays recoverable through the pinned frozen v5, which carried it in the generation that folded those findings. No provenance is lost.

attacksAttemptedAndFailed.attack: SATISFIED / QUALIFIED / implementation / G17 / minted recipes
attacksAttemptedAndFailed.detail: SATISFIED occurs five times, every one inside reviewGuidance instructions of the form 'Do not mark DR-122 SATISFIED'; there is no positive claim. QUALIFIED does not occur at all. All eight G17 occurrences record it as DROPPED or inapplicable per D-077/D-086, including the explicit 'does not resurrect G17'. Both docs/v2/implementation occurrences are denials. whatThisDoesNotDo carries 'Does not mint RunId/Finding recipes' and 'Does not mint a D9 code or exit number', and the produced-arm notes repeatedly mark runId, findingId and coverage as opaque DR-006 values 'not minted here'. Status is CANDIDATE-NOT-APPLIED, reviewStatus AWAITING-INDEPENDENT-REVIEW, sealRecommendation DO-NOT-SEAL, binds NOTHING.

I checked the verbatim claims against live bytes rather than trusting the labels. projectionTextCarriedVerbatim claims file 01 lines 108-133: 26 claimed lines against 26 actual, zero mismatches. registerRowQuoted claims the DR-122 row at file 08 line 304: that line does begin '| DR-122 |' and rowVerbatim matches it exactly. advisories.title: Claude v2 advisories ADV-SPC-V2-01/02/03 remain unfolded four generations later
advisories.detail: notFoldedThisSuccessor has carried 'Claude v2 advisories ADV-SPC-V2-01/02/03 remain not folded' since v2. The disclosure is honest and advisories legitimately travel, but four successors have now passed without disposition, which is the pattern by which an advisory quietly becomes permanent.
advisories.whyNotAFinding: Advisories are not ACCEPT bars in this corpus, the artifact discloses the residue rather than dropping it, and none of the three bears on the two repairs under review.
advisories.suggestedDisposition: A v7 should either fold them or record why they are being carried indefinitely, so the standing entry stops being load-bearing by default.
